methodology: RECONCILED after two rounds of isolated Codex AI review (round 1 against candidate 42304ec9d98862bafe18ffac52f28293a5f4430d; round 2 against candidate 77e45e38daebfc57194a3472d51564c97ac25e99). The governing evidence boundary, tightened in round 2, is now: each row's affirmative_architecture_split may cite only (a) content of the row's own evidence_scope anchor file (including its comments and docstrings), and (b) that same file's own direct local imports (module-level or function-scoped import statements written in the anchor file itself). A file discovered by finding who calls the anchor file (a reverse caller), by a repository-wide search/find for a plausibly-related file, or by opening a package-internal file that is not itself the direct target of an import statement (e.g. a schema file inside an npm-imported package whose import surface only exposes a client object) is NOT admissible as affirmative cross-module proof, even if it is real, relevant, and was in fact opened during investigation.

For each row, the applicable rule's required-evidence checklist (docs/packs/free-llm-v1-rule-contract.md) is applied to what is admissible per the boundary above: does the anchor file itself (its own content, or a file it directly imports) contain every element the checklist requires (file_local), does it concretely and admissibly establish that at least one required element is definitely not co-located, with a named, directly-imported (or in-file) second component (cross_module, non-ambiguous), or does neither hold within the admissible boundary (ambiguous)?

A row is recorded file_local only when every required element is textually present or locally defined in the anchor file itself. A row is recorded cross_module, non-ambiguous, only when a concrete second file is named via an admissible path (evidence_scope file content or its own direct import) and substantively relevant to a required element (an import present in the file but used only for something unrelated to the rule's checklist -- e.g. an unrelated output-directory constant -- does not count). A row is recorded ambiguous, with classification held at the conservative cross-module fallback and ambiguous=true, whenever the only available second-component evidence is a reverse caller, a same-package/same-directory sibling with no import statement connecting the two, a repository-wide search discovery, or a package-internal file not itself the import target -- even when that discovery is real and was actually inspected. Per round 2's reconciliation, this document now records 1 file-local, 18 confident cross-module, and 15 ambiguous rows; see review_and_reconciliation.rounds for the two review rounds that produced this result and source_access_accounting for which discoveries were admissible versus excluded.

No untouched-cohort artifact (calibration/llm/private/untouched-evidence.enc, any untouched-*/selection-untouched-* cohort file) was opened, listed, or referenced while producing this document. No detector, recognition logic, golden label, cohort manifest, rule, manifest, or prior v1.9 result file was run, modified, or relabeled.

This remains a structural, engineering-scoping conclusion about where in each repository the rule's decisive evidence physically lives, not a re-adjudication of any opportunity's present/absent ground-truth label, and not a recall/precision/accuracy claim about the detector.
